operations.text: Post-seating locking limits drift in a single-axis compression fixture

operations.expect: Three modes were tried with an existing pivoting compression pad. The components included a frame, a pin, a clamp, a pad and a lower platen. The records include nine rows. In the pitch condition, mode L had a force coefficient of variation of 2.3%, drift of 19 micrometres and seating time of 32 seconds. E had 7.2%, 12 micrometres and 18 seconds. In flat and roll conditions there were also differences. The fixture was operated at a preload of 10 N and a displacement of 0.20 mm. Repeatability and displacement during the ramp are discussed. These are constructed teaching records.
operations.text: An existing pivoting compression pad can accommodate a pitch slope, but remaining free during loading may permit drift. We compare locking before approach, remaining free, and locking under preload after seating. For a constructed 1° pitch example, post-seating locking reduced drift from 125 to 19 μm relative to remaining free, while seating time rose from 17 to 32 s. Force variation was 2.3%, versus 2.1% when free and 7.2% with early locking. Flat coupons gained no repeatability benefit, and cross-axis tilt remained uncorrected. Eight reseatings per coupon illustrate this tradeoff; they do not establish force accuracy.
